goal_text: (Reused from research_synth_013) Compare the Keynesian and Monetarist perspectives on the cause of recessions and the appropriate policy response. Address: diagnosis, prescription, and role of government.
ground_truth: Keynesians (Keynes, Samuelson) attribute recessions to insufficient aggregate demand and prescribe expansionary fiscal policy — government spending increases or tax cuts — viewing government intervention as essential in the short run. Monetarists (Friedman, Schwartz) attribute recessions to money supply contraction and volatile monetary policy, prescribing a stable, predictable monetary growth rule rather than discretionary intervention. Keynesians accept short-run trade-offs; monetarists emphasize long-run neutrality of money.
